bull.b: Growing subscription revenue and a larger production-app mix indicate customers are moving beyond experimentation toward recurring operational use. This can improve revenue visibility, deepen customer relationships, and create a scalable software and services layer alongside hardware sales.

The sharp increase in bookings and remaining performance obligations provides measurable commercial traction and a contracted revenue base. If delivered as scheduled, this backlog should support growth over the next several quarters and validate demand for D-Wave’s systems and services.

Peer-reviewed validation of high-fidelity, fast gate-model performance strengthens D-Wave’s technical credibility while its annealing platform is already commercial. A dual-platform approach broadens the addressable problem set and may help the company build an ecosystem before fault-tolerant systems mature.

bear.b: Continued operating cash consumption means growth is not yet self-funded and leaves the company reliant on its cash balance or external financing. This can constrain strategic flexibility and makes successful execution on commercialization and loss reduction essential over the medium term.

Losses are expanding as personnel and development investment rises, showing that commercial traction has not yet translated into operating leverage. Unless revenue scales faster than the cost base, sustained deficits could absorb resources and delay the path toward profitability.

Reliance on a small number of large system deliveries creates uneven revenue recognition and makes quarterly performance sensitive to installation timing. This volatility complicates planning, increases execution risk, and leaves near-term growth dependent on converting scheduled shipments into recognized revenue.
